name: Zapier MCP
description: Search knowledge across your apps and execute real-world actions by connecting Claude with the 9,000 apps on Zapier. Run workflows like sending emails, updating CRMs, scheduling meetings, and more, all within Claude.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
This server connects you to 9,000+ apps via Zapier.

IMPORTANT: Before calling any tool, ensure you have loaded the available tools from this server (tools/list).

If the user seems new or has no tools enabled, retrieve the "zapier:onboarding" skill using get_zapier_skill and follow its instructions.
Use list_zapier_skills to discover other saved workflows.

## Managing what's enabled

- `inspect_zapier_actions({ selected_api?, action?, tool_name?, params? })` — inspect enabled actions and resolve action parameter schemas. **Returns everything you need to build an execute call**: each action's `app` (display name), `selected_api`, `action` key, `action_type` (exact SDK type), `tool_name`, `params`, inline dynamic enum values when resolvable, and `dynamic_properties_schema` when parent values in `params` are sufficient.
- `discover_zapier_actions({ app? })` — search the Zapier app catalog for actions to enable (`app` is a free-text search query).
- `enable_zapier_action({ selected_api, app_display_name?, action? })` — add an action. Pass the `selected_api` returned by `discover_zapier_actions`.
- `disable_zapier_action({ selected_api, app_display_name?, action? })` — remove an action. Pass the `selected_api` from `inspect_zapier_actions`.

## Executing an action

Always call `inspect_zapier_actions` first to retrieve the action's exact `selected_api`, `action` key, `tool_name`, parameter schema, and any dynamic-argument guidance. Then:

1. If a parameter has `dynamic_enum_values`, use one of those `value` fields. If it has `dynamic_enum_missing_dependencies` or no usable value yet, set the dependency params you know and call `inspect_zapier_actions({ tool_name, params })` again. Use `enum_property`, `enum_search`, and `enum_cursor` with the same tool when you need to search or page one dynamic enum.

tool.description: Search 9,000+ apps to find actions you can enable. For authenticated services (Google Docs, Gmail, Sheets, Notion, Slack, Outlook, etc.), check here - generic web fetch tools cannot authenticate with these services. tool.name: inspect_zapier_actions
tool.description: Call `inspect_zapier_actions` first when you create a workflow or automation, before configuring a trigger or action for Gmail, Google Sheets, Google Drive, Slack, or any other app the user has connected, and before any execute_zapier_read_action or execute_zapier_write_action call. Call `inspect_zapier_actions` with no arguments first to list every enabled app with its exact `selected_api`; then call it again with one `selected_api` from that listing for the app's actions (`action`, `action_type`, `tool_name`), including the read action that samples a trigger, then with `tool_name` for one action's parameter schema. These apps handle OAuth automatically — use them instead of generic URL fetching for authenticated services. For a parameter flagged `is_dynamic_enum: true`, call `inspect_zapier_actions` again with `tool_name`, `enum_property`, and any parent values in `params` to resolve values. For actions with `dynamic_properties_depends_on`, settle those parameters first, then call this tool again with `tool_name` and `params` to get `dynamic_properties_schema`. To learn what an action returns, call `inspect_zapier_actions` with its `tool_name`, the same `params`, and `include_output_schema: true`; `output_schema` is the declared shape of the records, nested to match them. For a trigger, type the workflow's trigger input from it when a sample read returns no records. Sampled records win where they disagree, and declared types are advisory: a field declared as a string can arrive as a list. If the unfiltered listing has no entry for the app you need, you MUST call discover_zapier_actions next — NEVER say 'I can't do that' without checking discover_zapier_actions first. When you resolve a value from the user's request, matching a single record is not proof it is the one they meant: if their input is partial or ambiguous (e.g. a first name, or a search with several close matches), enumerate the candidates and let the user pick before passing a value to an execute call. Each app's `connections.default` names the account its actions run against. If that account doesn't fit the apparent context of the request (e.g. a personal address on a work task), flag it to the user before executing and note the account can be switched per action by passing a different `connection_id` (list the options with list_zapier_connections, or connect the right account via manage_zapier_connections) — do this even when only one account is connected.

tool.name: execute_zapier_read_action
tool.description: Execute a search or read action to get data from a connected app. REQUIRED: You MUST call inspect_zapier_actions first to get the exact action key, tool_name, and parameter schema. NEVER guess action names — they are NOT intuitive and WILL fail. If the app isn't enabled, use discover_zapier_actions then enable_zapier_action first. Pass exact argument values in `params`. For dynamic enum parameters, call inspect_zapier_actions again with `tool_name`, `enum_property`, and parent values in `params`. For actions with `dynamic_properties_depends_on`, call inspect_zapier_actions again with `tool_name` and settled parent params to learn `dynamic_properties_schema`. Before executing, be confident that every value in `params` correctly and uniquely identifies what the user asked for — especially fields naming a person, recipient, channel, account, record, or file. If the user gave only partial or ambiguous information (e.g. just a first name, or a term that could match several entities), do NOT assume a lookup that returns a single match is the right one: many lookups return one 'best' match even when others exist. Enumerate the candidates first — prefer a search or list action that can return multiple matches, or widen your query — and when more than one plausibly fits, present the options and let the user choose rather than guessing.

tool.name: manage_zapier_connections
tool.description: Manage an app's Zapier connections. Returns a URL the user can open to connect a new account, and optionally sets the app's default connection. An app REQUIRES a default connection before any of its actions can run. If the user has no default connection for the app they want to use, share the returned `auth_url` with them and ask them to tell you once they have added the connection; after they confirm, call list_zapier_connections to find the new connection's `connection_id`, then call this tool again with that value as `default_connection_id` to set it as the default. `selected_api` MUST come verbatim from discover_zapier_actions or inspect_zapier_actions — never guess or construct it (e.g. Gmail is `GoogleMailV2CLIAPI`, not `GmailCLIAPI`). If you don't already have it, call discover_zapier_actions first. To set the default account every action for this app should use, pass `default_connection_id` (look it up with list_zapier_connections). Share the returned `auth_url` with the user; after they finish, call list_zapier_connections to see the new connection.

tool.description: Saves a workflow as a reusable Zapier Skill — a good fit for multi-step workflows the user runs repeatedly or tool calls that always use the same parameters. For a high-quality skill: (1) action keys and parameter schemas should come from list_enabled_zapier_actions, (2) static values should be resolved up front (e.g. an email to a Slack user ID), (3) any ambiguity about targets, recipients, or scope should be resolved with the user before creation, (4) known parameter values are pre-filled; only runtime-computed parameters are left bare. Re-using results from earlier in the conversation avoids redundant calls.

skillDefinition.description:
Full markdown skill definition.

BEFORE writing this definition, ensure the following have been done (skip any step whose results are already available from earlier in this conversation):
1. list_enabled_zapier_actions called for each app involved — to get exact action keys and parameter schemas.
2. User-specific configuration gathered — project keys, channel names, default assignees, recurring values.
3. Ambiguities resolved — if the workflow has unclear targets, recipients, or scope, ASK the user before proceeding. E.g. 'DM the user in the list, or DM you?', 'Which Jira project?', 'Send to the channel or to you directly?'
4. Static values resolved and validated — e.g. email resolved to a Slack user ID via a lookup action.

If any of these were already done earlier in the conversation, reuse those results. Do NOT repeat calls you have already made.

STRUCTURE the skill definition with these sections:
- Title and one-line description
- '## Validated fixed values' — all static IDs, names, keys discovered or confirmed during creation
- '## Actions' — each ZapierAction reference with the FULL parameter signature. Quote every param value that is known and fixed. Leave bare only params that must be computed at runtime.
- '## Runtime instructions' — numbered steps for execution
- '## Constraints' — what the agent must NOT do (e.g. do not re-resolve known IDs)

Reference each Zapier action inline with:
ZapierAction[app:action](param: "locked_value", dynamic_param)

Use the exact `app` and `key` values from list_enabled_zapier_actions.
Quoted param values are locked and forwarded directly at execution.
Bare param names are filled by skill logic at runtime.

IMPORTANT: Maximize locked params. Every param that CAN be resolved at creation time MUST be quoted. The goal is zero unnecessary API calls at runtime. Leverage any action results, user IDs, or parameter values already obtained in this conversation.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Zapier MCP to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Zapier MCP to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.zapier.com/api/v1/connect. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: Is Zapier MCP MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Zapier MCP scores 84/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan does not yet meet ChatGPT publishing checks and does not yet meet Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Zapier MCP's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Zapier MCP scores 75/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 17 of 17 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Zapier MCP?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Zapier MCP in automation-workflows on the Manufact MCP catalog include Sidewave Maggiordomo, Corsair Cloud, Fleet Workspace, Whalesync, and typenode-mcp.

_published_faq.name: Does Zapier MCP MCP require authentication?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zapier MCP requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.

_published_faq.name: How can Zapier MCP improve its MCP documentation?
